notes: The intermediary was checked: FB4's Parameters_official.csv (github.com/jim-breck/FB4, saved as docs/research_notes/fetched/v2/fb4/Parameters_official.csv) has a row 'Largemouth bass (adult), Rice et al. 1983' — CEQ 2, CA 0.33, CB −0.325, CQ 2.65, CTO 27.5, CTM 37, REQ 1, RA 0.008352, RB −0.355, RQ 0.0313, RTO 0.0196, RK1 1, ACT 1, BACT 0, SDA 0.15848, FA 0.104, UA 0.08817, ED 4184 — identical to the code's bioJuv for catfish and bass. Three things for the rewrite: (1) FB4's note on that row reads 'SDA & UA reflect use of (C − F) instead of C; corrected RA & RQ', so the distributed set is not exactly the 1983 paper's: cite it as 'Rice et al. 1983, as corrected and distributed in FB4 (Deslauriers et al. 2017)'; (2) FB4 labels the set LifeStage 'adult', while the model uses it only for young fish (< 30 g bullheads, < 30 g or < 250 g smallmouth), so the paper should say it is applied outside its labelled stage; (3) the paper's Table 4.3 gives 250 g for smallmouth but src/species.js has juvW 30 g (src/w3/fish3.js sets 250 under stageR5) — say which version the table describes. Reeve et al. 2025 (Table 1) independently lists RA 0.008352, RB −0.355, RQ 0.0313, RTO 0.0196 as 'the Rice et al. (1983) model' and found it predicts the highest winter consumption (p 0.62 against 0.37 from loggers).
